title: North Bayou F80: Is This Budget Gas-Spring Monitor Arm Worth It?
summary: The North Bayou (NB) F80 is the best-known budget gas-spring monitor arm: VESA 75/100, height, tilt, swivel and portrait rotation, desk clamp or grommet mount. The catch is the load rating — retailers list anything from 2–6.5 kg to 2–9 kg — and monitors that are too light don't work either. Here's how to tell whether yours fits.
description:
## Who is it for?

- Owners of tilt-only monitors (ASUS TUF VG249QE5A, Xiaomi G24i and similar) who want height adjustment and portrait mode.
- 22–27-inch VESA 75/100 monitors weighing roughly 2–6.5 kg without the stand.
- Small desks that need the space under the screen.

## Why consider it?

- Gas-spring height adjustment, tilt, swivel and 360° rotation for a very low price.
- Clamp or grommet mounting, with cables routed inside the arm.
- Sold worldwide in black and white, so it's easy to find and return.

sections.title: What is the North Bayou F80?
sections.content:
North Bayou — usually branded **NB** — is a Chinese maker of low-cost monitor mounts, and the **F80** is its best-known single gas-spring arm. It's simple: a short post clamps to the back edge of the desk, a lower arm swivels around it, and an upper arm with a gas spring raises and lowers the screen. The end of the arm carries a VESA 75/100 plate that screws into the back of the monitor.

The F80's appeal is price. North Bayou doesn't publish an official list price, retail prices vary a lot from one seller and region to the next, and it is often discounted — but it consistently sits at the bottom of the gas-spring arm market. For that money you get what many budget monitors don't offer: height adjustment, portrait rotation and the desk space under the screen back.

One naming caution: marketplace listings in some regions lump the F80 into titles alongside other model codes. Zero Technology couldn't confirm those are the same product, and lookalike arms from other brands are common. This review covers the genuine **NB F80**.

sections.title: Load capacity: the spec that matters most (and that sellers disagree on)
sections.content:
A gas-spring arm only works inside its weight range. Too heavy and the monitor slowly sinks; too light and the arm pushes it back up even with the tension fully backed off. Retailers don't agree on the F80's range:

- **2–6.5 kg, 17–27 in:** Zylax (Australia), Newegg Canada, Staples Canada.
- **2–9 kg, 17–30 in:** Woolworths (Australia), Umart, and Amazon listings quoted by Frontdeskreview (9 kg / 19.8 lb).

We're not going to pick the nicer number. The sensible reading is that **6.5 kg is the comfortable limit** and 9 kg is a best case. Owner feedback points the same way: one eBay buyer says the arm handles a 24-inch monitor well, but with a Dell P2717H 27-inch "any bump on the desk" starts it sinking, and they disagree that it's really a 27-inch arm. On the other hand, the long-term owner behind Limteam's review runs a 27-inch monitor on an F80 "without any wobble or flex." The difference is likely the individual monitor's weight and how carefully the tension was set.

The other end of the range gets less attention: **the roughly 2 kg minimum**. The Xiaomi G24i, for example, weighs 3.0 kg *including* its base (Xiaomi), so the panel alone is noticeably lighter. Weigh your monitor without its stand — or look for the "weight without stand" figure on the manufacturer's spec page — and make sure it sits comfortably inside the range on the listing you buy from. If you'll add a monitor light bar or webcam on top, count that weight too.

sections.title: Adjustment range and real ergonomic benefit
sections.content:
Zylax and Newegg Canada list about **250 mm** of height travel, **+35° to −50°** tilt, roughly 180° swivel and 360° rotation; other listings and Limteam quote +85° to −30° tilt and 260 mm. Either way, the F80 covers the three adjustments most people actually need:

- **Raising the top of the screen to eye level** — something the tilt-only stands on the ASUS TUF VG249QE5A and Xiaomi G24i can't do. Limteam's author credits the arm with easing their neck and back pain.
- **Portrait mode** for code, long documents and logs.
- **Pushing the screen back or swinging it aside** when you need a clear desk for writing, drawing or a big mouse pad.

Know the limits, though. Frontdeskreview ranks its 10-inch height adjustment as the **lowest of the 11 arms** it compared. That's fine at a normal sitting desk, but tall users at a standing desk, or anyone stacking a monitor above a laptop, may run out of travel. The F80 also has one short lower arm rather than a long double-jointed reach, so it won't pull a monitor far forward from the desk edge the way premium arms do. MyByWays, who owns both the F80 and North Bayou's H80, adds that the F80's swivelling lower half can sweep items off the desk, and there's nowhere to store the Allen key.

sections.title: Installation: check your desk before you check the arm
sections.content:
The F80 mounts with a **C-clamp** on the desk edge or **through a grommet hole**, both confirmed in the F80 manual on Manuals+. North Bayou doesn't publish a clear maximum desk thickness for this model; one US retailer lists about 3.1 inches (79 mm), which we couldn't verify against manufacturer documentation. Before buying, check:

- **A solid, rigid edge.** Thin particleboard, glass tops and hollow-core desks don't cope well with the leverage of a monitor held out from the post. A steel or hardwood plate under the clamp spreads the load.
- **No crossbar or drawer** directly under the clamp position.
- **Room behind the desk.** The arm clamps at the back edge; if your desk is against a wall, the arm still needs space to swing. If you also want a clamp-on pegboard, the two clamps will compete for that edge — see the comparison below.

Once the monitor is attached, you must **adjust the spring tension** with the Allen key to match the monitor's weight. Skipping this is why many first-time users conclude the arm "sinks" or "springs up." Limteam found the install relatively straightforward while noting that some users struggle; budget 15–30 minutes.

sections.title: F80 variants, other North Bayou arms and how it fits with other gear on this site
sections.content:
**Within North Bayou's range:**

- **F80 / F80W** (this review): the same arm in black or white.
- **FP80:** a laptop-tray version instead of a VESA plate — a different product, so read the listing carefully.
- **H80:** a pole-style mount with a mostly fixed arm height. MyByWays owns both and prefers the H80's finish, though moving it along the pole needs tools.
- **F100A:** a double-extension arm for 22–35-inch screens (Memory Express) — the step up for larger, heavier monitors.
- **F160:** a dual-monitor arm for two 17–27-inch screens.

**With monitors reviewed on Zero Technology:**

- **ASUS TUF Gaming VG249QE5A:** VESA 100, 3.3 kg with stand (ASUS), tilt-only stand — the most natural F80 pairing.
- **Xiaomi G24i:** VESA 75, 3.0 kg with base (Xiaomi), tilt-only. It mounts, but confirm the bare panel stays above the ~2 kg minimum.
- **VSP IP2705F (27-inch):** VESA 100, but retailers don't clearly publish its weight, so weigh it before buying an arm.

**With other desk-setup gear:** a clamp-on desk pegboard and the F80 both want the back edge of the desk, so measure for both and remember the F80's lower arm sweeps behind the monitor. A monitor light bar such as the Sidohome SG301 rides on top of the screen and moves with the arm — convenient, but it adds a little load to the spring.

sections.title: Who should buy it — and who shouldn't
sections.content:
**Buy it if you:**
- Have a 22–27-inch VESA 75/100 monitor weighing roughly 2–6.5 kg without its stand.
- Use a tilt-only stand (ASUS VG249QE5A, Xiaomi G24i and similar) and want height and portrait adjustment without replacing the monitor.
- Have a small desk and want the space under the screen for a keyboard, a large mouse pad or a notebook.
- Want the cheapest credible gas-spring arm.

**Skip it if you:**
- Use a 34-inch ultrawide, a large curved monitor or a heavy 27–32-inch screen near 7–9 kg — get a higher-capacity arm such as NB's F100A or a premium arm.
- Use a very light monitor (portable displays, some ultra-slim models) under about 2 kg.
- Have a glass, thin particleboard or hollow desk, or a crossbar right under the edge.
- Need a lot of height (standing desk, tall user) or long forward reach.
- Have a monitor without VESA holes — adapters exist but add wobble.

sections.title: Sources for this review
sections.content: Zero Technology has **not used** the North Bayou F80 in person. This review is compiled from: international retailer listings at Zylax, Umart and Woolworths (Australia) and Newegg and Staples (Canada) for load, screen size, tilt and height travel; the F80 manual on Manuals+ (mounting options); Frontdeskreview's spec comparison (sourced from Amazon data, not a hands-on test); long-term owner write-ups by Limteam and MyByWays; and buyer feedback on eBay. Sources disagree on load capacity (2–6.5 kg vs 2–9 kg), screen size and tilt range — we've flagged each and recommend the more conservative figures. North Bayou has no complete official international product page, so the photos come from international retailer listings (The Wires Zone, AHW Store). Updated November 2026.

sections.title: Should you buy the North Bayou F80?
sections.content: Yes — provided your monitor sits comfortably inside the load range. The F80 is the cheapest way to turn a tilt-only monitor into a setup with height adjustment, portrait mode and a clear desk, and on a 24-inch VESA 100 monitor like the ASUS VG249QE5A it's about the most worthwhile upgrade you can bolt on. Our 8.0 score (down from the 9+ this page previously carried) reflects the real limits: inconsistent load ratings, heavier 27-inch monitors that can sink when the desk is bumped, short height travel and budget-level finish. If your monitor weighs more than about 6.5 kg, is an ultrawide, or your desk is weak, spend more on a higher-capacity arm rather than pushing the F80.

pros: Very low price for a gas-spring arm — far cheaper than buying a monitor with a height-adjustable stand.
Turns tilt-only stands (ASUS VG249QE5A, Xiaomi G24i) into height, swivel and portrait adjustment.
Supports both VESA 75 and 100, covering most mainstream 24–27-inch monitors.
Clamp or grommet mounting, with cables routed inside the arm.
Sold worldwide in black and white, so it's easy to buy and return.
A long-term owner (Limteam) reports a 27-inch monitor held without wobble and no noticeable gas-spring wear after years.
cons: Retailers disagree on load capacity (2–6.5 kg vs 2–9 kg), screen size and tilt range.
There's a minimum load of about 2 kg — very light monitors can spring back up.
One eBay buyer reports a Dell P2717H 27-inch sinking whenever the desk is bumped.
Height travel of 250–260 mm ranks lowest of the 11 arms Frontdeskreview compared.
The swivelling lower arm can knock things over, and there's no Allen-key holder (MyByWays).
Maximum desk thickness isn't clearly published, and the bright yellow logo is conspicuous (Limteam).
buying_advice: Great value if your monitor's weight fits the range

faq.question: How much weight can the North Bayou F80 hold?
faq.answer: Listings differ: 2–6.5 kg (Zylax, Newegg Canada) or 2–9 kg (Woolworths, Amazon listings). Treat 6.5 kg as the comfortable limit and weigh your monitor without its stand before buying.

faq.question: Will it hold a 27-inch monitor?
faq.answer: Usually, if the monitor is light enough. Limteam's author runs a 27-inch without wobble, but an eBay buyer found a Dell P2717H 27-inch sinking when the desk was bumped. Heavy 27-inch or large curved monitors deserve a higher-capacity arm.

faq.question: Can a monitor be too light for it?
faq.answer: Yes. The minimum is about 2 kg, below which the spring pushes the screen up even at the lowest tension. The Xiaomi G24i, for example, is 3.0 kg with its base, so check the bare panel weight.

faq.question: Is it a good match for the ASUS VG249QE5A or Xiaomi G24i?
faq.answer: Both have tilt-only stands and benefit a lot. The ASUS (VESA 100, 3.3 kg with stand) is the most natural fit; the Xiaomi (VESA 75, lighter) works too, but confirm it isn't under the minimum load.

faq.question: Can I use it alongside a clamp-on desk pegboard?
faq.answer: Yes, if the back edge of your desk has room for both clamps and the F80's lower arm can swing freely. Put the arm on one side and the pegboard on the other, and measure first.

faq.question: What's the difference between the F80, F80W and FP80?
faq.answer: The F80 and F80W are the same arm in black and white. The FP80 has a laptop tray instead of a VESA plate and isn't meant for monitors.
